newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks snap winning streak.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks snap winning streak.

text.p: Argentine stocks succumbed to mild profit-taking Tuesday after a long upward march but traders said the tone remained firm.

"A pullback was inevitable, so we can't complain -- nobody had quite taken in the 11-day rise because it was very mild-mannered and didn't generate any turbulence," said Gabriel Ruiz of brokers Tavelli.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.5 percent to close at 765.29. It had gained 6.3 percent in the previous 11 sessions, breaking down technical resistance and reaching a five-year high.

"There are still pessimists out there who expect the market to fall," Tavelli said. "But they are looking at factors like the trade deficit and U.S. interest rates, which are no longer really relevant."

He said the skeptics would be persuaded Argentina remained a good buy once they noted the strong economic growth potential revealed by the latest indicators, the consolidation process taking place in the banking sector, the likelihood of a trade surplus by the end of the year, the huge amount of funds handled by mutual funds and pension funds and the low political risk ahead of October mid-term elections.
"Argentina depends less and less on foreign cash flows, but this is not reflected yet in the markets," Tavelli said.

The bolsa's all-share index dipped 0.2 percent, with losers outstripping winners 31 to 14 and 22 stocks closing flat. Floor volume rose to 20.8 million pesos from 12.6 million Monday, when the U.S. Memorial Day holiday caused local markets to grind nearly to a halt, while over-the-counter turnover totaled 94.6 million pesos.
"Offers dried up as prices eased today, which means we should be able to stay more or less steady tomorrow even with U.S. long bond yield above 7.0 percent," one dealer said.

Best main-tier performers were food giant Molinos, which rose 2.6 percent, carmaker Sevel, up 1.5 percent, and banks Banco Frances, Bansud and Banco de Galicia, which rose 1.7 percent, 1.0 percent and 1.0 percent, respectively. Traders said the bank sector was boosted by news Banco Santander had bought a controlling stake in Banco Rio de la Plata and would issue its stock on the local and New York bourses shortly.
The day's biggest MerVal losers were steelmaker Acindar, textile and footwear firm Alpargatas and oil company Astra, off 2.1 percent, 1.7 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
